_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for XOM retrospectives (retro/build_xom.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2008 were accepted before the open or during the session on their release days (each print's release_time says which). The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), and the latest declared dividend. ExxonMobil's fiscal year is the calendar year. It gives no earnings, revenue, volume or margin guidance in numbers in any filing of the period (releases, 10-Qs, 10-Ks and the analyst-meeting 8-Ks: production outlooks as charts and words, a multi-year capital range), so 'guides' is empty and the no-guide rules apply. Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest filing that reports it, per share as published (the 2001 two-for-one split restates the years published before it: 'eps_published', 'shares_published'), and the company's earnings per share excluding special items replace GAAP EPS where a filing publishes them (the history's 'normalization' says which). Revenue is total revenues and other income, the one revenue line the releases publish. A print's growth rates and margin are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw'; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago quarter is the one the same release shows. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

history_vintages.why: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil and gas business is fundamentally a commodity business. This means the operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the world may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on gasoline and other refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among the factors it lists, 'the competitiveness of alternative hydrocarbon or other energy sources' and 'laws and regulations related to environmental or energy security matters, including those addressing alternative energy sources and the risks of global climate change' (its own FY2006 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'XOM'): the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, is 1997-2006; no 10-K published by then reports 1996 on the merged Exxon Mobil basis (the FY1999 10-K's income statements and operating summary start in 1997), so each signal has the nine year-on-year changes 1998-2006 (rule T takes the annual values the filings report). Each change comes from the latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years: total revenues and other income and income before income taxes from its income statement, volumes from its operating summary. Everything as reported, seams included (the 2002 discontinued-operations reclassification, the 2006 netting of purchases/sales with the same counterparty, which the FY2006 10-K applies to 2002-2006 petroleum product sales, and the merger divestments of 2000).
